### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 345f0b154cbdbce771eb40d33f722cf4b48050d1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `7055150823ac7416bdcf4c2bb8d20cb1c17050b0`
Local-runs: none

Face: test-only card, `Clause-②: no` on the card's claim and on the PR body; the diff touches no published schema, no governed path and declares no narrowing, so no contract-tier face is hit and this is the dispatching seat's `TIER_DEFAULT` review of record. Inputs read: card #25207 (body, claim 6342189035, dev report 6343554273), #24343's acceptance section, the PR body, its file list, its net diff against merge base `123ff6f4e2fa`, and the check-runs on the head above (read at 2026-10-22T15:15Z).

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) Test-only for real: correct.** Net diff against the merge base is one added file, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/signup-organization-census-walled.dogfood.test.ts` (+251 / -0); two commits, both inside it. `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`, so nothing published moves; the PR carries `skip-changeset` and no changeset, which is this repo's form for a test-only diff. The file imports packages by name only and reads nothing outside its package, so no cross-package input is hidden.
- **(b) The walled leg covers what the card asks: correct.**
  - Both postures: one boot per posture in a loop over `group` and `isolated`, `multiTenant: 'posture-only'`, with `AuditPlugin` and `EmailServicePlugin` composed in one stack.
  - The journey is all there: the admin opens the audience; the registrant self-registers (verification mail) and creates an organization (first membership); then they invite a second stranger (invitation mail), who signs up and accepts (first membership).
  - The census is derived at run time, not from a hand list: `sqlite_master` plus `PRAGMA table_info` on the store, re-read on every call, so date-named activity shards and new tables join on their own. The short list in the guard is a minimum-reach floor, not the census.
  - The whole-store leg asserts 0 rows with NULL or empty `organization_id`, boot rows included. A second leg asserts every row the journey wrote names `orgId`: the store is snapshotted by `table/id` after the admin's settings write.
  - Each writer is also pinned on its own: the grant (one `member_default` grant, owned by the organization; the invitee holds none), activity about each grant and about the invitation mail, no activity about org-less `sys_user`, the invitation in `sys_email` owned by the organization, and verification mail in `sys_identity_email` (no column, checked by PRAGMA) and absent from `sys_email`.
  - This meets #24343's first acceptance bullet (0 NULL on the three writers' tables, or no column) and the card's "Wanted" list. The PR body says #24343's second bullet (the ceremony `advisory` count) is out of scope.
- **(c) The NULL leg vs. the ablation: the acceptance is met honestly. The NULL leg is a floor, not the detector, and the PR says so.**
  - The NULL assertion cannot go red under the class of fault the card names. With 38 of 39 tenant columns NOT NULL and D9 refusing a stamp-less walled system write, a writer that loses its stamp leaves no row, not a NULL row. The dev measured this and put it in the PR body ("Why the existence legs matter") and in the file header (lines 32-36). It is not a hidden vacuous green.
  - What turns red is the existence legs. The reported ablation (the grant writer's `organization_id` replaced by an undefined global, marker confirmed in the built `dist`, then restored to a byte-identical blob and preflighted `--absent`) read `4 failed | 11 passed`: the grant-writer and activity-writer legs, in both postures, with the engine's D9 refusal named in the log. The `single` control stayed green.
  - Each of the other two writers has its own existence leg that reds the same way: an absent invitation mail fails `invitationMail?.id`, absent activity fails `about.length > 0`, and verification mail misrouted into `sys_email` fails the `tenantMail` leg.
  - So "an ablation turns it red" holds for the file. That is the checklist's accepted case: the literal criterion is overturned by a stronger measured invariant, and the overturn and its measurement are written in the PR body.
  - The NULL leg is not wholly vacuous either: it also catches an empty-string stamp (which NOT NULL does not stop), the one nullable column (`sys_sso_provider`), and any future migration that makes a column nullable again. But it is a regression floor. It is ⛔ not evidence that the writers stamp, and no one should cite it as that.
- **(c) Robustness: acceptable.**
  - Posture guard: pinned per boot (`tenancy.posture === posture`, `degraded === false`, `isolationActive === true`).
  - Env and cleanup: `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE` is set before each boot and restored in `afterAll`, and the stack is stopped there.
  - No collisions: e-mail addresses and slugs are unique per posture.
  - No timing race: the writers run inside awaited engine hooks (`triggerHooks('afterInsert')` is awaited in objectql; the deferred grant lands on the awaited first-membership hook). No ordering depends on wall time, and the journey-row set is keyed by `table/id`, not by order.
  - Two small soft spots, non-blocking:
    1. `storeRows` keys rows on `id`, so a tenant-column table without an `id` column would collapse to one key and could hide a row (none is known in this store).
    2. The census reads only the datasource that serves `sys_user`. In this composition that is the whole platform store.
- **(d) The `single` leg is untouched: correct.** It is a sibling file. `signup-organization-census.dogfood.test.ts` is not in the diff and no helper is shared.

### ② Semver level

None. The diff publishes nothing (private package, test file only), so no changeset is owed. `Check Changeset` on the head: **success** (job 119887608476 passed at its live label re-read on `skip-changeset`; the duplicate run 119889504885 is `skipped`). This matches the declared `Clause-②: no`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The claim and label writes were done by the card thread itself (the dev's first deviation):** answered, consistent. Exactly one `Claim:` is on the card (6342189035), and it names the PR's branch. The card's events show `pm:dispatched` added, `pm:queue` removed and `os-bill` assigned in the same minute. The PR assignee mirrors the card. `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` is green on the head. No second claim is owed and none should be posted.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally:** answered from CI. Its step "Every published require entry point actually loads" in `Build Core` (job 119887863576, head `7055150823`) concluded **success**. The test-only diff cannot move it in any case.
- **PR attribution line:** answered, accepted. The top link points to the card thread, as that session's own context requires verbatim. The footer is the session-URL form AGENTS.md prescribes for PR bodies. No model identifier appears in the body or in either commit's trailers (`Claude-Session` + `Co-authored-by: Claude`).
- **Sibling file instead of a second `describe` (third deviation):** accepted. The claim's file surface allowed it.
- **Wall time (acceptance note, `Duration 33.90s`):** noted, not a flag. The 10 s file line is measured on runs that exclude `@objectstack/dogfood` (`measure-test-shard-timings.mjs`), and no `test-budget` class fits a real-stack boot.
- **Observation for landing:** `Dogfood Regression Gate (n/3)` is skipped on `pull_request` by design (full battery only). This file's first CI execution is therefore `main`'s full battery after merge. The only run evidence before landing is the dev's local run at this head. A red there is this lane's main-red.
- **Closing keywords:** `Fixes #25207` (the card is fully delivered) and `Part of #24343` (no verb next to the number). `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green.
- `open_questions`: none were raised.

Check-runs on the head at posting: 47 in total. 33 `success`, 12 `skipped` (the opt-in and full-battery legs, plus a duplicate `Check Changeset`), 0 failure, and 2 still reading `in_progress`. Those two are `Test Core (5/6)` (job 119887863686) and `Lint · ESLint` (job 119887610617). Every step of each, `Complete job` included, concluded `success` at 14:39Z and 14:40Z, but the check-run status never closed. All five required contexts read `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (aggregate), `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Before queueing, the landing seat should re-read the two stuck runs. This verdict does not stand in for them.

The PR body and the file header state it with the measurement; the card's acceptance ("an ablation turns it red") is met by the file.
